lawyer: Mr. Md. Mozammel Hoque, Advocate ------ for petitioner.
parties:
Kuleshar Barman alias Kakaru Barman
Vs.
Sree Naresh Chandra Barman and others
full_judgment: 2. Short facts for disposal of the rule are that on 20.5.84 the petitioner made an application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for pre-emption of the land transferred by his full brother, opposite party no. 4, to the opposite parties No. 1-3 by a deed of sale executed on 5.2.81 and registered on 26.7.82. Before the transfer no notice under section 89 of the said Act was served upon the petitioner. The purchasers are strangers to the holding. Case of the pre-emptor is that before sale, case land was transferred by his brother to him on the basis of an oral purchase on receipt of Taka 3,000/-and possession was delivered to him. On 22.3.84 when he was dispossessed by opposite parties no. 1-3 on the representation that they purchased the land, the petitioner for the first time came to know about the sale and on obtaining certified copies of the deed of transfer on 29.3.84 became sure about the transfer.
